# infrawrench_dora_settings (Resource)

How the organization's DORA metrics (the Delivery page, `infrawrench dora`, the weekly digest's Delivery line) decide what is production and what counts as a failed change.

An organization **singleton**. There is no DELETE on this route, so `terraform destroy` leaves the stored settings as they are.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# What the Delivery page's DORA metrics count as production, and how soon after
# a change an incident or rollback counts it as failed.
resource "infrawrench_dora_settings" "this" {
  failure_window_hours    = 24
  production_environments = ["production", "prod*"]
  pipeline_patterns       = ["*deploy*", "release"]

  count_failed_deploys     = false
  include_resource_changes = false
  digest_enabled           = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `count_failed_deploys` (Boolean) Count a production deploy that itself failed as a failed change.
- `digest_enabled` (Boolean) Include the Delivery line in the weekly digest.
- `failure_window_hours` (Number) Hours after a production change in which a declared incident or a rollback counts the change as failed, 1-720. An incident is blamed on the most recent matching change in the window only.
- `include_resource_changes` (Boolean) Count changes observed by sync (the change timeline: console edits, drift) as changes too. A reverted one counts as failed.
- `pipeline_patterns` (List of String) CI pipeline names whose runs count as deploys (Buildkite, CircleCI, GitLab and Bitbucket runs are only counted when they match), at most 50 patterns of 1-100 characters. `[]` counts no pipeline runs. Each pattern is matched case-insensitively and `*` is the only wildcard. The server trims patterns and drops duplicates, so write each once and without surrounding spaces, or the saved list will differ from the configuration.
- `production_environments` (List of String) Environment names that count as production, 1-50 patterns of 1-100 characters, e.g. `["production", "prod*"]`. Each pattern is matched case-insensitively and `*` is the only wildcard. The server trims patterns and drops duplicates, so write each once and without surrounding spaces, or the saved list will differ from the configuration.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The organization id. DORA settings is an organization singleton, so this is the only value it ever takes and it is what `terraform import` addresses.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# An organization singleton: there is only ever one, and it has no id of its
# own, so it imports under the organization id.
terraform import infrawrench_dora_settings.this org_01HXYZABCDEF
```
